message.content:
Los Angeles (Pacific Time) is **9 hours behind** Berlin (Central European Time) most of the year.  
Because both regions observe daylight‑saving time, the offset can shift:

| Period | Los Angeles | Berlin | Difference |
|--------|-------------|--------|------------|
| Standard time (winter) | UTC‑8 | UTC +1 | **9 h** |
| When U.S. DST starts before German DST | UTC‑7 | UTC +1 | **8 h** |
| When German DST starts before U.S. DST ends | UTC‑7 | UTC +2 | **9 h** |
| When German DST ends before U.S. DST ends | UTC‑7 | UTC +1 | **8 h** |
| After U.S. DST ends | UTC‑8 | UTC +1 | **9 h** |

So, unless you’re looking at a specific date during the overlapping DST transition windows, you can safely say Los Angeles is 9 hours behind Berlin.
